source_text: Λογιζόμενος δέ τις, ὡς καλὸς μὲν ὁ ἥλιος, ἡδὺς δὲ οὗτος ὁ βίος, ἀγαθὸν δὲ καὶ τὸ πολυχρόνιον γενέσθαι διαπαντὸς εὐφραινόμενον, καὶ ὡς φοβερὸν ὁ θάνατος, καὶ ἀΐδιον κακὸν, καὶ εἰς τὸ μηδὲν ἄγων, οἴεται χρῆναι, πάντων μὲν ἀπολαύειν τῶν παρόντων καὶ δοκούντων ἡδέων. Συμβουλεύει δὲ καὶ τοῖς νέοις, τῇ ἑαυτῶν ὥρᾳ καταχρῆσθαι ἀνέντας τὰς ἑαυτῶν ψυχὰς εἰς πᾶσαν ἡδονὴν, καὶ χαρίζεσθαι μὲν ἐπιθυμίαις, πράττειν δὲ τὰ αὐτοῖς δοκοῦντα, καὶ βλέπειν τὰ τέρποντα, καὶ ἀποστρέφεσθαι τὰ μὴ οὕτως ἔχοντα. Πρὸς ὃν τοσοῦτον λέξω· Ὅτι ἀνοηταίνεις, ὦ οὗτος, μὴ προσδοκῶν τὴν ἐφ᾽ ἅπασι τούτοις ἐκ Θεοῦ κρίσιν ἐσομένην. Πονηρὸν δὲ ἀσωτία καὶ ἀσέλγεια, καὶ ῥυπαρὰ σωμάτων ἡμετέρων ὕβρις ὀλέθριος. Νεότητι μὲν γὰρ ἄνοια παρέπεται· ἄνοια δὲ ἄγει εἰς ὄλεθρον.
thought_title: Answer to the pleasure-seeker: God will judge
orientation: Solomon answers the pleasure-seeker who urges the young to indulge themselves: God will judge all these things.
pass_a_gloss: Someone reckoning that the sun is beautiful/fair, and this life sweet, and good also to become long-lived rejoicing continually, and that death is fearful and an everlasting evil, and leading into nothing, thinks it necessary to enjoy all the present things and the seeming-pleasant things. He advises also the young to use fully their own season/prime, having let loose their own souls into every pleasure, and to gratify desires, to do the things seeming good to them, and to look at the delighting things, and to turn away from the things not so. To whom I will say so much: That you are senseless, O you, not expecting the judgment from God that will be upon all these things. Evil is profligacy and licentiousness, and filthy outrage of our bodies is destructive. For senselessness accompanies youth; and senselessness leads into destruction.

pass_b_english: Someone reasons that the sun is fair (Ecclesiastes 11:7) and this life is sweet, that it is good to live a long time and rejoice all the while (Ecclesiastes 11:8), and that death is fearful, an everlasting evil that brings one to nothing. So he thinks that one ought to enjoy everything that is present and seems pleasant. He also advises the young to make full use of their prime, letting their souls loose into every pleasure, to gratify their desires, to do whatever seems good to them, to look at whatever delights them, and to turn away from whatever does not (Ecclesiastes 11:9).

To him I will say only this: You there, you are out of your senses, for you do not expect the judgment that will come from God for all these things (Ecclesiastes 11:9). Profligacy and licentiousness are evil, and the filthy abuse of our bodies is deadly (Ecclesiastes 11:10). For senselessness follows close on youth, and senselessness leads to ruin (Ecclesiastes 11:10).
notes: Metaphrase of Ecclesiastes 11:7-10. Voice: the first paragraph reports another man's reasoning and advice (λογιζόμενός τις ... οἴεται ... συμβουλεύει); it is not Solomon's counsel. Solomon answers from 'To him I will say'. ὦ οὗτος is a blunt address ('you there'). Ecclesiastes 11:9 is cited twice: once for the pleasure-seeker's advice, which restates the first half of the verse, and once for the judgment, which restates its second half. 'Abuse' renders ὕβρις (outrage, violation). No Psalm citations.
